UNIL – AI Provider Due Diligence Checklist (version 3.2)
Version 3.2 · 27 October 2026 · working document to be validated (see annex 4)
Legend
● PROCEED: continue
● SUBJECT TO CONDITIONS: continue subject to a condition (including measures to establish, plan, negotiate or complete)
● DO NOT PROCEED: blocking point
● PATH INFORMATION: no verdict; the answer indicates what follows (question, procedure or obligation)
Question badges:
• AI ACT: based on the AI Act (rules below).
• HIGH RISK: asked only if the tool is high-risk under the AI Act.
• PERSONAL DATA: asked only if personal data are processed.
Structure: questions are numbered within each stage; answer choices are a), b), c), etc.
Source order and navigation rules
1. STAGE 0 – Legal scope (NIST AI RMF: Govern)
2. STAGE 1 – UNIL: data and compliance (Map)
3. STAGE 2 – UNIL: AI tool (Map)
4. STAGE 3 – UNIL: public procurement procedure, sections A–C
5. STAGE 4 – Supplier: eligibility, section D
6. STAGE 5 – Supplier: data and security (Measure)
7. STAGE 6 – Supplier: AI tool (Measure)
8. STAGE 7 – Supplier: contract, section E
9. STAGE 8 – Summary and decision (Govern, Manage)
10. STAGE 9 – Operation and monitoring, section F (Manage)
Rules:
• Without a routing arrow, proceed to the next question.
• An answer containing “→ Go to…”, “→ Proceed…” or “→ Ask…” indicates where to continue or which questions to display.
• A blocking answer stops the assessment, except under the AI ACT rule below; proceed directly to source stage 8 to record the decision.
• A conditional answer allows continuation; its condition and recommendation are carried into stage 8.
• AI ACT and HIGH RISK questions: if the AI Act does not apply (stage 0, question 1(b)), they remain as good practice and blocking answers become conditions. This also covers blocking answers dependent on HIGH RISK marking (stage 4, question 6(c); stage 5, question 17(b)).
• HIGH RISK questions are asked only for a high-risk tool (stage 2, question 2(a) or (b)).
• PERSONAL DATA questions are asked only if personal data are processed (stage 1, question 3(c) or (d)).
• Supplier answers (stages 4–7) must be capable of being accompanied by evidence (an attachment).
• All opinion requests (DPO, legal service, IT security officer) are carried into stage 8, question 3.
